This was the U.S. military's codename for its multinational campaign against the Islamic State across Iraq, Syria, and Libya — which campaign?
Operation Inherent Resolve: Military intervention against the Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant.
He named his B-29 bomber after his mother, then flew it over Hiroshima to drop the first atomic bomb used in warfare. Who was this Army Air Forces pilot?
Paul Tibbets: United States Air Force general (1915–2007)
This Mexican president founded the party that would dominate the country for decades, then ruled as de facto leader during a period called the Maximato. Who was he?
Plutarco Elías Calles: President of Mexico from 1924 to 1928.

Known as Bilqis in Arabic and Makeda in Ge'ez, this Hebrew Bible figure brought a caravan of lavish gifts to King Solomon and is linked by modern historians to an ancient South Arabian kingdom in Yemen?
Queen of Sheba: Historical figure in the Abrahamic religions.
A central tenet of Hinduism, Buddhism, Jainism, and Sikhism, this idea holds that an immortal soul never disperses at death but passes into a newborn baby or an animal. What's the concept?
Reincarnation: Concept of rebirth in different physical form.
Notorious for humiliating defendants and handing down frequent death sentences, this German judge presided over the People's Court from 1942 to 1945 — who is he?
Born in Paris to a family of Georgian political refugees, this career diplomat became the first woman ever elected president of her adopted country — who is she?
Sparked by a succession crisis after King Frederick VII died heirless, Prussian and Austrian troops crossed into a Danish-controlled duchy in February 1864 — which 19th-century conflict?
Second Schleswig War: War between Denmark, Prussia, and Austria in 1864.

Formed in 2022 after a leadership split within a major Maharashtra party, this faction led by former chief minister Uddhav Thackeray was given a new 'Flaming Torch' symbol by India's Election Commission — which party?
Shiv Sena (UBT): Political party in Maharashtra, India. Shiv Sena (Uddhav Balasaheb Thackeray) (ISO: Śiva Sēnā (Uddhava Bāḷāsāhēba Ṭhākare); lit. 'Army of Shivaji, led by Uddhav Thackeray'; abbr.
Sparked in 1898 by the sinking of the USS Maine in Havana Harbor, this brief conflict handed the U.S. control of Puerto Rico, Guam, and the Philippines — what was it?
Spanish–American War: 1898 conflict between Spain and the United States.
Active from 1973 to 1975, this American far-left militant group kidnapped newspaper heiress Patty Hearst and had six members die in a 1974 Los Angeles shootout with police — which group?
Symbionese Liberation Army: American militant organization (1973–1975). The three surviving fugitives recruited new members, but nearly all of them were apprehended in 1975 and prosecuted.
Elected archon in 493 BC, this populist Athenian politician championed naval expansion, fought at Marathon, and became Athens's leading statesman ahead of the second Persian invasion — who is he?
Themistocles: Athenian politician and general (c. 524–459 BC)
This Haitian general rose from a slave rebellion to become Governor-General-for-life of Saint-Domingue before ultimately clashing with Napoleon's troops. Who was he?
Toussaint Louverture: Haitian general and revolutionary (1744–1803)
Armenia's first Defence Minister, he had just become prime minister in 1999 when he was assassinated that October — who was he?
Vazgen Sargsyan: Armenian military commander, politician (1959–1999)
According to medieval European legend, this immortal man taunted Jesus on the way to the Crucifixion and was cursed to roam the Earth until the Second Coming — who is this legendary figure?
The last president to have served in the Civil War — the only one to start as an enlisted man — he led the U.S. through the Spanish-American War before his 1901 assassination; which president was he?
William McKinley: President of the United States from 1897 to 1901.

Commonly known by a compass-direction nickname, this state existed from 1962 until unifying with its southern neighbor in 1990, having been formed when officers toppled a monarchy and sparked an eight-year civil war — which country?
Yemen Arab Republic: Country in West Asia (1962–1990)
A pharmacist by training and MP for Manisa since 2011, which Turkish politician has led the Republican People's Party since 2023?
Who among these was born first?
Patrick Geddes (born 1854) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these people was born first?
Patrick Geddes (born 1854) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four began earliest?
COBOL (founded 1959) is the earliest of the four. COBOL (Common Business-Oriented Language;) is a compiled English-like computer programming language designed for business use.
Which of these four came first?
MATLAB (founded 1984) is the earliest of the four. MATLAB (Matrix Laboratory) is a proprietary multi-paradigm programming language and numeric computing environment developed by MathWorks.
Who among these is a physicist?
Which of these is a mathematician?
Emmy Noether is a mathematician. Amalie Emmy Noether (23 March 1882 – 14 April 1935) was a German mathematician who made many important contributions to abstract algebra.
What is the atomic number of Meitnerium?
Meitnerium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Mt and atomic number 109.
What is the atomic number of Rubidium?
Rubidium is a chemical element; it has symbol Rb and atomic number 37.
In what year was Pope Benedict XVI born?
Pope Benedict XVI: Following his resignation, he chose to be known as "pope emeritus", a title he held until his death on 31 December 2022.
In what year was Javier Milei born?
Javier Milei: Javier Gerardo Milei (born 22 October 1970) is an Argentine politician and economist who has served as the 57th president of Argentina since 2023.
In what year was Piero Ferrari born?
Piero Ferrari (born Piero Lardi, 22 May 1945; later Piero Lardi Ferrari) is an Italian billionaire businessman and sport personality.
In what year did Giordano Bruno die?
Giordano Bruno: Bruno's pantheism was not taken lightly by the church, nor was his teaching of metempsychosis regarding the reincarnation of the soul.
In what year did Erwin Schrödinger die?
Erwin Schrödinger: Schrödinger shared the 1933 Nobel Prize in Physics with Paul Dirac "for the discovery of new productive forms of atomic theory".
In what year was Silicon discovered?
Silicon (SILL-ih-kən) is a chemical element; it has symbol Si and atomic number 14.
Which company manufactures Antonov An-124 Ruslan?
Antonov An-124 Ruslan: Aviastar-SP. The An-124 remains the largest military transport aircraft in service.
In which country is Mil Mi-8?
Mil Mi-8: Burkina Faso. The Mi-8 is the world's most-produced helicopter, with over 17,000 units used by over 50 countries.
Who is credited with discovering Antlia?
Antlia: Nicolas Louis de Lacaille. Antlia (from Ancient Greek ἀντλία) is a constellation in the Southern Celestial Hemisphere.
Who is credited with discovering Factitious disorder imposed on another?
Factitious disorder imposed on another: Roy Meadow. The victim is typically the caregiver's child but is occasionally an adult partner.
Who is credited with discovering Trisomy 18?
Trisomy 18: John H. Edwards. Trisomy 18, also known as Edwards syndrome, is a genetic disorder.
Who is credited with discovering Strontium?
Strontium: William Cruickshank. Strontium is a chemical element; it has symbol Sr and atomic number 38.
A "classic organochlorine" insecticide once heavily used to treat seed and soil, it was banned in most countries by the 1990s after proving a persistent, bioaccumulating pollutant. What is it?
Aldrin is an organochlorine insecticide that was widely used until the 1990s, when it was banned in most countries.
This deep-tissue swelling — of the face, tongue, throat, or limbs — comes on within minutes to hours and is driven by either histamine or bradykinin — what is it?
Angioedema is an area of swelling (edema) of the lower layer of skin and tissue just under the skin or mucous membranes.
With almost 500 species in the daisy family, this large plant genus includes mugwort, wormwood, and sagebrush, and is sometimes confused with a related genus of sages — which genus?
Artemisia (plant) (art--) is a large, diverse genus of plants belonging to the daisy family, Asteraceae, with almost 500 species.
Which SI unit of radioactivity honors the scientist who co-discovered the phenomenon alongside the Curies?
Becquerel (symbol: Bq) is the unit of radioactivity in the International System of Units (SI).
In this distributed ledger, each record carries a cryptographic hash of the one before it, so altering any block would mean rewriting every block that follows — what is this technology called?
Blockchain is a distributed ledger with growing lists of records (blocks) that are securely linked together via cryptographic hashes.
This English guard-dog breed combines the size of the Mastiff with genes from the extinct Old English Bulldog, and gained Kennel Club recognition in 1924 — which breed?
Bullmastiff is an English breed of dog of mastiff type and large size, with a solid build and a short muzzle.
This Mexican business magnate was ranked the richest person in the world by Forbes from 2010 to 2013, building his fortune through a sprawling conglomerate called Grupo Carso. Who is he?
Carlos Slim (born 28 January 1940) is a Mexican business oligarch, investor and philanthropist.

Sold under the brand name Thorazine, this phenothiazine antipsychotic treats schizophrenia and bipolar disorder — but it's also been used for nausea, pre-surgery anxiety, and even stubborn hiccups. What is it?
Chlorpromazine (CPZ), marketed under the brand names Thorazine and Largactil among others, is an antipsychotic medication.

This highly venomous, nocturnal snake, black or bluish-black with narrow white crossbands, is widely distributed across South Asia, from grasslands to agricultural fields to human settlements — what snake is it?
Common krait (Bungarus caeruleus) is a highly venomous snake species belonging to the genus Bungarus in the family Elapidae.

Named for a mythological Greek youth who was transformed into a tree after accidentally killing a beloved stag, this genus of evergreen conifers is considered polyphyletic by modern genetic analysis — what genus is it?
Cupressus (common name cypress) is one of several genera of evergreen conifers within the family Cupressaceae; for the others, see cypress.
Caused by a Corynebacterium bacterium, this infection can spin a tough grey 'pseudomembrane' across the throat that slowly chokes off the airway — what is it?
Diphtheria is an infection caused by the bacterium Corynebacterium diphtheriae. The pseudomembrane can grow to cover a wide area of the throat, leading to strangulation and death.

This scientific and engineering discipline uses transistors, diodes, and integrated circuits to control and amplify the flow of electric current, converting between forms like AC to DC. What is the field called?

Electronics is a scientific and engineering discipline that studies and applies the principles of physics to design, create, and operate devices that manipulate electrons and other electrically charged particles.
This sweet-tasting but toxic diol is a workhorse of antifreeze and polyester manufacturing, and astronomers have even detected the molecule in space — what is it?
Ethylene glycol (IUPAC name: ethane-1,2-diol) is an organic compound (a vicinal diol) with the formula (CH2OH)2.

Also known as Lasègue–Falret syndrome after the pair of psychiatrists who first described it, this shared delusional disorder is named for the small number of people who typically experience it together — what is it called?

Folie à deux (French for 'madness of two'), also called shared psychosis or shared delusional disorder (SDD), is a rare psychiatric syndrome in which symptoms of a delusional belief are "transmitted" from one individual to another.

A Belgian-British emigrant to New York, this inventor struck gold during a 1906 stay in Central America by perfecting an early instant-coffee process and building a company to mass-produce it — who was he?
George Washington (inventor) (May 20, 1871 - March 29, 1946) was a Belgian-British inventor and businessman.

These common coastal seabirds, most closely related to terns and skimmers, were once known by an older name still surviving in some English dialects and cognate with the German word Möwe — what birds are they?
Gull (see Taxonomy), are seabirds of the subfamily Larinae.
First identified in 1910, this organic compound is stored in mast cells and basophils and, though not made by classic endocrine glands, still acts as a local hormone — what compound is it?
Histamine is an organic nitrogenous compound found in mammals and many vegetables, fruits and food products.

This phenomenon describes how a system's state depends on its history, as when a magnet holds different moments depending on past field changes — it underlies memory in a hard disk drive. What is it called?
Hysteresis is the dependence of the state of a system on its history. Hysteresis can be found in physics, chemistry, engineering, biology, and economics.

This English mathematician made foundational contributions to matrix and invariant theory, founded the American Journal of Mathematics at Johns Hopkins, and was teaching at Oxford when he died. Who was he?
James Joseph Sylvester (3 September 1814 - 15 March 1897) was an English mathematician.
Honored across Asia as a model healer and "Medicine King," this 5th-century BCE physician of Rajgir tended to King Bimbisāra — and to the Buddha himself. Who was he?
Jīvaka was the personal physician of the Buddha and the Indian King Bimbisra.
Shaped by constitutions and produced through statutes, regulations or judicial precedent, this body of enforced rules governs behavior and shapes politics and society — what is it?
Law is a set of rules that are created and enforced by governmental or societal institutions to regulate behavior, with its precise definition a matter of longstanding debate.

This American four-engine turboprop military transport aircraft is a comprehensive update of an older Cold War-era design, and remains the only version of its lineage still in production, with 500 delivered to 26 operators. What aircraft is this?
Lockheed Martin C-130J Super Hercules is a medium-size American four-engine turboprop military transport aircraft.
Often found combined with iron in minerals, this hard, brittle, silvery transition metal is added to stainless steel to improve strength and wear resistance. What element is it (symbol Mn)?
Manganese is a chemical element; it has the symbol Mn and atomic number 25.
This scientific field studies Earth's atmosphere and short-term weather phenomena, with a central focus on forecasting — name the discipline?
Meteorology is the scientific study of the Earth's atmosphere and short-term atmospheric phenomena (i.e., weather), with a focus on weather forecasting.
Named for the river near which its type fossil was found by a Dutch chalk quarry in the 18th century, this genus of marine reptile lived until the end of the Cretaceous — what is it?
Mosasaurus ("lizard of the Meuse River") is the type genus (defining example) of the Mosasauridae, an extinct group of aquatic squamate reptiles.

An English aeronautical engineer who wrote novels like On the Beach and A Town Like Alice, he adopted a pen name specifically so his employers at Vickers wouldn't think him 'not a serious person.' Who is he?
Nevil Shute (17 January 1899 - 12 January 1960) was an English novelist and aeronautical engineer who spent his later years in Australia.
In this learning process, voluntary behaviors grow more frequent through reinforcement or fade through punishment and extinction — what is it called?
Operant conditioning is a learning process in which voluntary behaviors are modified by association with the addition (or removal) of reward or aversive stimuli.
Combining medicine with comedy, this physician organizes volunteers to clown around for orphans and patients worldwide through a nonprofit institute he founded in 1989 — who is he?
Patch Adams (born May 28, 1945) is an American physician, comedian, social activist, clown, and author.

Sitting at the intersection of textual criticism, literary criticism, history, and linguistics, this scholarly discipline studies language through oral and written historical sources — what is it called?
Philology (from Ancient Greek (philologa) 'love of word') is the study of language in oral and written historical sources.
This birth defect results in extra fingers or toes, occurs more often in the hands than the feet, and has been linked to more than three dozen genetic mutations — what is it?
Polydactyly (commonly known as sixth finger and extra finger) is a birth defect that results in extra fingers or toes.

This medical specialty diagnoses, treats, and prevents disorders of cognition, perception, mood, emotion, and behavior, typically beginning assessment with a case history and mental status exam — name the field?
Psychiatry is the medical specialty devoted to the diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of deleterious mental conditions.
What dimensionless quantity in fluid dynamics, expressing the ratio of inertial to viscous forces, determines whether a flow will be smooth and laminar or chaotic and turbulent?
Reynolds number (Re) is a dimensionless quantity that helps predict fluid flow patterns in different situations by measuring the ratio between inertial and viscous forces.
A Stanford physicist who also held an English literature degree, in 1983 she became, at 32, the youngest American ever to fly in space. Who is she?
Sally Ride (May 26, 1951-July 23, 2012) was an American astronaut and physicist.
Domesticated well over 3,000 years ago and grown widely in India, Myanmar, and Sudan today, this plant is considered one of the oldest oilseed crops known to humanity — what is it?
Sesame (Sesamum indicum) is a plant in the genus Sesamum, also called benne.
Native to a swath from Ireland to southern China, this aromatic herb is used to flavor food and herbal teas, and its extracted oil serves as both a flavoring and a scent — what is it?

Spearmint (Mentha spicata), also known as garden mint, common mint, lamb mint and mackerel mint, is native to Europe and southern temperate Asia, extending from Ireland in the west to southern China in the east.
The fifth most common element on Earth, this multivalent nonmetal usually turns up in sulfide and sulfate minerals and is a bright yellow crystalline solid — what is it?
Sulfur (American spelling or sulphur (Commonwealth spelling) is a chemical element; it has symbol S and atomic number 16.
Discovered independently by two chemists in 1861 via its distinctive green spectral line, this silvery-white metal takes its name from the Greek word for a green shoot or twig — what element is it?
Thallium is a chemical element; it has symbol Tl and atomic number 81.

This androgenic anabolic steroid, part of the nandrolone group, is marketed in ester forms for veterinary use — commonly given to livestock to boost muscle growth and appetite — what's the steroid called?
Trenbolone is an androgen and anabolic steroid (AAS) of the nandrolone group which itself was never marketed for human use.

This flowering plant genus, the largest in its family with over 680 species, is found mostly across the temperate Northern Hemisphere but also as far-flung as Hawaii and the Andes. What is this plant commonly called?
Viola (plant) is a genus of flowering plants in the family Violaceae.
Common across Europe and also found in Asia, this large carpenter bee bores its nest into dead wood rather than building a hive — which species?
Xylocopa violacea is the common European species of carpenter bee, and one of the largest bees in Europe.
Taken by mouth, smeared as a cream, or injected, this antiviral medication is a frontline treatment for herpes simplex, chickenpox, and shingles. What is it?
Aciclovir: Antiviral medication used against herpes, chickenpox, and shingles.
A broad-spectrum benzimidazole drug, it clears out an alarming roll call of intestinal parasites — pinworm, hookworm, ascariasis, giardiasis and more. Which medication is it?
The heaviest member of its family, this Southeastern U.S. reptile sees males stretch up to 15 feet and tip 1,000 pounds — and it's the larger of just two surviving species in its genus. What is it?
American alligator: Crocodilian native to the Southeastern United States.
First described by a German entomologist in 1818 and known as the 'marsh mosquito,' this genus is the only one that transmits malaria to humans — which genus is it?
Anopheles: Genus of mosquito. The genus Anopheles diverged from other mosquitoes approximately 100 million years ago (mya), and, like other mosquitoes, the eggs, larvae, and pupae are aquatic.
Its guanidino group serves as the biological precursor for nitric oxide production, and this amino acid earned the one-letter code 'R' purely for phonetic reasons — what is it?
Arginine: Amino acid. Arginine is the amino acid with the formula (H2N)(HN)CN(H)(CH2)3CH(NH2)CO2H.
This category of illness occurs when the body's adaptive immune system mistakenly attacks its own healthy tissue, with more than 80 recognized forms identified so far — what's the category?
Autoimmune disease: Disorders of adaptive immune system. Autoimmune diseases are a separate class from autoinflammatory diseases.
Coming on over about 48 hours, this temporary facial paralysis droops one side of the face and can heighten sensitivity to sound — what condition is it?
Bell's palsy: Facial paralysis. Bell's palsy is a type of facial paralysis that results in a temporary inability to control the facial muscles on the affected side of the face.

Despite its name, this African animal's hide actually ranges from brown to grey, and it's distinguished from its 'white' cousin by a pointed, hooked upper lip rather than a wide, square one — which species?
Black rhinoceros: Species of mammal. Although the species is referred to as black, its colours vary from brown to grey.
Named for its unusually long forelimbs — Greek for 'arm lizard' — this Late Jurassic sauropod was first described in 1903 from fossils found in Colorado — which dinosaur?
Brachiosaurus: Sauropod dinosaur genus from the late Jurassic Period.
Caused by the SARS-CoV-2 coronavirus, this disease triggered a global health emergency declared by the WHO in March 2020 and lifted in May 2023 — which disease?
COVID-19: Contagious disease caused by SARS-CoV-2. Starting in January 2020, the disease spread worldwide, resulting in the COVID-19 pandemic.

This group of heart-muscle diseases includes the 'broken heart syndrome' type and can lead to irregular heartbeats, fainting, or even sudden cardiac death — what's the general term for this condition?
Cardiomyopathy: Disease of the heart muscle. In dilated cardiomyopathy the ventricles enlarge and weaken.
Also known as an ischemic stroke, this necrotic brain condition is the second-leading cause of death worldwide and a leading cause of physical disability — what is it?
Cerebral infarction: Stroke resulting from lack of blood flow.
Every animal in this group shares five telltale traits — including a notochord, pharyngeal slits, and a tail that extends past the anus — at some stage of life; which of these belongs to that phylum?
Chordate: Phylum of animals having a dorsal nerve cord.
Also nicknamed the 'Maybug' or 'doodlebug,' this European scarab beetle's males swarm during mating season while females stay put munching leaves that release telltale scent chemicals — which beetle?
Cockchafer: Species of scarab beetle. The cockchafer develops via metamorphosis, in which the beetle undergoes stages of eggs, larvae, pupae and adults.
These colonial marine invertebrates secrete calcium carbonate to build the hard skeletons that form tropical reefs — what are they?
Coral: Marine invertebrates of the subphylum Anthozoa.
Named for the ancient Greek word for a ship's helmsman, this transdisciplinary field studies feedback loops and circular causal processes across engineering, biology, and social systems — what is it?

Cybernetics: Study of circular causal processes. Cybernetics' transdisciplinary character means that it intersects with a number of other fields, resulting in a wide influence and diverse interpretations.
This medical and surgical specialty treats everything from inflammatory conditions and cancers to hair loss, requiring about four years of training beyond medical school — what field is it?
Dermatology: Field of medicine dealing with the hair, nails, skin, and its diseases.
Developed from the civilian DC-3 airliner and nicknamed 'Dakota' by the RAF, which WWII transport plane hauled troops, cargo, and paratroopers for roughly 100 countries' militaries?
Douglas C-47 Skytrain: Military transport aircraft derived from DC-3.

This Russian political scientist studies authoritarian governance and legislative process, taught at Moscow institutions for nearly a decade, and by 2022 had a YouTube channel with a million subscribers — who is she?
Dubbed 'the father of nuclear physics,' this New Zealander won a Nobel Prize in Chemistry despite proposing that atoms have a tiny, densely charged nucleus — who is he?
Ernest Rutherford: New Zealand physicist and chemist (1871–1937)
Beloved in gardens for gobbling up pests, this spiny mammal native to Iberia and Scandinavia was introduced to New Zealand in the late 1800s but is now Red Listed in Britain — what is it?
European hedgehog: Species of small spiny mammal.
Also called slapped cheek syndrome, this common childhood illness is caused by parvovirus B19, discovered in 1975 — what condition is it?
Fifth disease: Red rash due to infection with parvovirus B19.
Known online by the alias TiAMO, this Swede co-founded a notorious file-sharing site and stood trial for it in 2009, a saga captured in the documentary TPB AFK — who is he?
This field studies how geography shapes international relations and foreign policy, though critics have dismissed its early theories as pseudoscience — which discipline?
Geopolitics: Study of geography's effects on politics.
With DNA up to 99% identical to ours, this troop-dwelling great ape — led by a dominant 'silverback' — is the largest living primate on Earth — what is it?
Gorilla: Genus of large African apes.
First described in 1893 during a flu pandemic and mistakenly blamed as its cause, this Gram-negative bacterium causes pneumonia and meningitis mainly in infants — which bacterium?
Haemophilus influenzae: Species of bacterium. The bacteria are mesophilic and grow best at temperatures between 35 and 37 °C.
Introduced to Britain in the 19th century as an ornamental plant, this Caucasus-native's sap causes painful blistering burns when exposed skin meets sunlight — which species?
Heracleum mantegazzianum: Species of flowering plant. Heracleum mantegazzianum, commonly known as giant hogweed, is a monocarpic perennial herbaceous plant in the carrot family Apiaceae.

In the Renaissance this field of study covered classical literature and language rather than religion or divinity, and today it groups subjects using critical and interpretive methods rather than empirical ones — what broad academic category is this?
Humanities: Academic disciplines that study society and culture.

Dubbed the 'saviour of mothers,' this Hungarian doctor proved in 1847 that hand-washing with chlorinated lime solutions could drastically cut deadly childbed fever at a Vienna maternity clinic — who is he?
Ignaz Semmelweis: Early pioneer of antiseptic procedures.
Native to South America but planted worldwide for its long-lasting violet blooms, this tree — also called the black poui — is listed as Vulnerable in its wild range by the IUCN. What is it?
Jacaranda mimosifolia: Species of sub-tropical tree.
This British physicist shared the 1951 Nobel Prize with Ernest Walton for first splitting the atomic nucleus — a feat that opened the way to nuclear power and weapons. Who was he?
Defined by a carbon-oxygen double bond flanked by two carbon groups, this class of organic compound includes acetone and gives some sugars and steroids like testosterone their structure — what is it?
Ketone: Organic compounds of the form >C=O.
Native to the Mediterranean and used to season food as a bay leaf, this aromatic evergreen prominent in classical Greco-Roman culture can grow up to 20 metres tall — what is its scientific name?
Laurus nobilis: Species of flowering plant in the laurel family Lauraceae.
Nearly always affecting women, this incurable condition causes fat buildup in both legs that's resistant to typical weight loss and often mistaken for other circulatory disorders — what is it?
Lipedema: Condition involving excessive deposition of fat in the legs.
The sole member of its genus in the soapberry family, this sweet, mildly tart fruit carries a distinctive rose-like aroma and comes in Indochinese, Philippine, and Javanese subspecies — what is it?

Often making people tall and thin with long fingers and very flexible joints, this connective-tissue disorder carries serious risks to the heart and aorta — caused by a mutation in the FBN1 fibrillin gene — which condition?
Marfan syndrome: Genetic disorder involving connective tissue.

Fever, a fierce headache, neck stiffness, and a telltale rash that doesn't fade when a glass is rolled over it can signal this inflammation of the membranes around the brain and spinal cord — what is it?

Meningitis: Inflammation of membranes around the brain. Meningitis (pl. meningitides) is acute or chronic inflammation of the protective membranes covering the brain and spinal cord, collectively called the meninges.
Developed for the Soviet Union, this swept-wing jet fighter dominated early dogfights in the Korean War and prompted the US to rush its F-86 Sabre into combat — which aircraft?
Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-15: Soviet fighter aircraft. The MiG-15 was one of the first successful jet fighters to incorporate swept wings to perform near Mach 1.

Prized by gourmet cooks yet toxic if eaten raw or undercooked, this genus of honeycomb-capped edible fungi is difficult to cultivate, making wild harvests a multimillion-dollar industry — which fungal genus?
Morchella: Genus of fungi. Morchella, the true morels, is a genus of edible sac fungi closely related to anatomically simpler cup fungi in the order Pezizales (division Ascomycota).
Sold under the brand name Deca-Durabolin, this anabolic steroid is prescribed for conditions like anemia and osteoporosis despite masculinizing side effects — which compound?
Nandrolone: Androgenic Anabolic steroid. Nandrolone, also known as 19-nortestosterone, is an endogenous androgen.
Humphry Davy coined this colorless gas's cheerful nickname for the euphoria it brings, and it still earns a spot on the WHO's Essential Medicines list for dentistry and surgery. What is it?
Nitrous oxide: Colourless non-flammable greenhouse gas.

The most widely cultivated species of its genus, this bulb vegetable counts garlic, leeks and chives among its close relatives, and the shallot was reclassified as merely a variety of it in 2011 — what is it?
Onion: Bulbous vegetable. The shallot is a botanical variety of the onion which was classified as a separate species until 2011.
Nicknamed the 'scaly anteater,' this nocturnal mammal is covered in keratin scales and slurps up ants and termites with a long tongue — which animal?
Pangolin: Mammals of the order Pholidota.
A famous singer known for her CCTV New Year's Gala appearances, she has served as China's First Lady since 2012 as the wife of its paramount leader — who is she?
Peng Liyuan: First Lady of China since 2012. Peng also sang the theme songs of several popular TV series, such as The Water Margin (1998).
With a phosphate-charged head and two fatty-acid tails joined by glycerol, this molecule builds neuron membranes and can decline up to 20% by age 80 — what is it?
Sitting less than a degree from the north celestial pole, this yellow supergiant is famously steady for navigation — but is secretly a triple star system. What is it?
Polaris: Northern pole-star; brightest star in Ursa Minor.

Diagnosed in about 8% of male urology visits in the US, this umbrella term covers several bacterial and non-bacterial pelvic conditions, despite its name not always involving actual inflammation — which condition?
Prostatitis: Medical condition. Prostatitis is an umbrella term for a variety of medical conditions that incorporate bacterial and non-bacterial origin illnesses in the pelvic region.
Named partly for Jack Northrop, designer of a tailless aircraft, which genus of enormous azhdarchid pterosaur is a top candidate for the largest flying animal ever?
Quetzalcoatlus: Genus of azhdarchid pterosaurs from the Late Cretaceous.
Native to East Asia but a notorious invasive pest in Europe and North America, this knotweed has won over beekeepers and foragers alike, its young stems tasting of lemony rhubarb. What plant is it?
Native to Eurasia and commonly known simply as the raspberry, this red-fruited bramble is widely cultivated across temperate regions — what species is it?
Nicknamed 'snail fever,' this tropical disease is caused by a parasitic flatworm picked up from freshwater contaminated by infected snails — what is it?
Schistosomiasis: Human disease caused by parasitic worms called schistosomes.
The first woman on Facebook's board, she turned the company profitable as its long-serving COO and founded LeanIn.Org — who is she?
Once called 'hyposulphite of soda,' this reducing agent treats cyanide poisoning and served as photography's key fixer in the 19th century — what compound?
Sodium thiosulfate: Chemical compound. Sodium thiosulfate (sodium thiosulphate) is an inorganic compound with the formula Na2S2O3·xH2O.
For 30 years this English theoretical astrophysicist held Cambridge's most prestigious academic post—the Lucasian Professor of Mathematics. Who?
